A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeNIe and GeNIe-Ada research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original few-shot, long-tailed, and fine-grained classification experiments, noise ablations, and generated-image analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, diffusion-backbone tests, computation controls, and class-probability analyses.

M1.justification: Partial noising, contradictory target prompting, and adaptive selection after the largest projected embedding shift remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Alternative diffusion engines and noise grids are evaluated as experimental configurations without revising the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mini-ImageNet, tiered-ImageNet, ImageNet-LT, CUB200, Cars196, Food101, and FGVC-Aircraft under the same task coverage. Added analyses and model configurations introduce no distinct dataset, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds DAFusion and PDA+Net/Meta-DM to few-shot comparisons, and Cap2Aug, VL-LTR, zero-shot CLIP, and additional ResNet-50 long-tail comparators. It removes older comparison rows, including Delta-Encoder/SNCA from Table 1 and Transd-CNAPS/FEAT from Table 2. The relocated tiered-ImageNet ResNet-34 comparison also gains MAML+dist and ProtoNet rows.

E3.justification: New protocols include CLIP ResNet-50/VL-LTR training, SDXL-Turbo and SD3 evaluations, and SVM class-probability analysis. Appendix A.4 tests three adaptive noise levels against twice as many Txt2Img samples for approximate compute matching. DAFusion uses only the first 100 episodes, and SDXL-Turbo uses 10 diffusion steps. These supplement the retained original evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds classifier-confusion analysis using source/target probability distributions (Figure 6 and Appendix A.1), robustness checks across diffusion engines (Table 5), a computation-control experiment (A.4), and an unprompted/same-class/contradictory-prompt case study (A.5). These substantially extend tests of sample hardness, generality, and computational fairness. Existing Figure 5 is reduced from six example rows to two.

E5.justification: The main few-shot evaluations retain 95% confidence intervals over 600 mini-ImageNet and 1000 tiered-ImageNet episodes. Added result rows continue the existing uncertainty-reporting practice, without introducing seeds, independent repeated-run reporting, significance tests, or a new estimation procedure. DAFusion's smaller evaluation subset is a protocol difference.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for new comparators, diffusion engines, and the computation-control setting. Its new ResNet-50 long-tail block reports GeNIe-Ada at 59.5% Few and 71.5% overall accuracy; the original LiVT results remain 52.7% and 63.1%. Shared few-shot augmentation results and Table 4 are retained. Original SD1.5 values in Table 5 differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: The projected-distance formula and adaptive-selection mathematics are unchanged. Neither version adds formal guarantees or proofs; the new probability plots and computation calculations are empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The central hard-negative augmentation and classification-performance claims remain. v3 adds an explicit first-to-our-knowledge claim for combining contradictory information through noise adjustment, and removes the introduction's explicit spurious-correlation use case while emphasizing few-shot and long-tailed classification.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the hardness explanation by connecting classifier-probability overlap and oracle label consistency to decision boundaries, beyond v2's semantic-shift argument. It adds interpretations of diffusion-engine generality and prompt-dependent context preservation. Runtime limitations now distinguish offline suitability from real-time constraints, while v2's explicit Figure 4 caveat that feature preservation was untested is removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents DAFusion's 5000 embedding-optimization iterations per class and VL-LTR implementation details, including four hours on eight RTX 3090 GPUs. Original LiVT hyperparameters move intact to Appendix A.3, and the code-access statement remains unchanged. The measured 4.4/6.7-second per-image generation timings in v2 are removed.

R1.justification: v3 expands discussion of previously cited DAFusion work and adds references including Cap2Aug, textual inversion, BLIP, Meta-DM, and VL-LTR. It sharpens distinctions from caption- and LLM-guided augmentation, while retaining the underlying positioning around hard negatives generated from contradictory information.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten, with explicit contribution bullets. Related Work moves ahead of the method, and the conclusion becomes Concluding Remarks containing limitations and broader impact. Appendix organization expands substantially, and author ordering changes.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different page layout and redistributes tables and figures. Original Figure 4 examples are merged into v3 Figure A4, while the new main Figure 4 selects earlier appendix examples. Figure 5 is shortened, Table 5 gains diffusion-model blocks, and new probability plots, a prompt-comparison figure, and a computation-comparison table are added.

improvement.justification: The new DAFusion/Cap2Aug comparisons, SDXL-Turbo/SD3 tests in Table 5, and approximate compute-matched experiment in Appendix A.4 substantially strengthen evidence about relevant competitors, generator dependence, and computational fairness. These address important validation gaps in v2 while retaining its main benchmark results. Budget matching remains approximate, and averaged probability-distribution overlap does not justify A.1's claim of proving decision-boundary proximity. These limitations and the loss of precise generation timings do not outweigh the substantial empirical strengthening.
